The resettlement action plan of December 2010 was defined in the financing agreement as setting out the compensation, physical relocation and assistance for people displaced by the project. The same schedule required the utility to keep a Kabeli Project Unit for the whole of implementation, headed by a project manager and staffed with people whose experience, qualifications and terms of reference had to satisfy the Association at all times (Section I.A).

The same paragraph required the ministry to keep the project executing unit staffed until the project was finished with named specialists, among them a social and resettlement specialist, and to maintain a project directory committee that met at least every four months and sent its minutes to the Bank.

manila-sewerage-site-clearances-san-mate.conditions_add: The project agreement of 22 July 2005 required Manila Water Company to carry out the project in accordance with the environmental management plan, the resettlement action plans and the land acquisition, resettlement and rehabilitation policy framework in a manner satisfactory to the Bank, to send any proposed change to those documents to the Bank for prior approval, and from 30 June 2006 to have an independent agency audit compliance with them each year (World Bank, Project Agreement for Loan 7311-PH, Schedule 2, paragraph 3). For one named site the agreement set a condition on the works themselves: the company could not start building the sewage treatment plant at Tapayan unless the people displaced by the dike and pond works there "have been compensated and rehabilitated in accordance with a resettlement action plan, satisfactory to the Bank" (Schedule 2, paragraph 5). The Bank lent the money to Land Bank of the Philippines "only on condition that" the Republic of the Philippines guarantee the borrower's obligations, and the Republic also undertook to take all actions needed, through the Department of Public Works and Highways, to carry out that resettlement action plan (Guarantee Agreement for Loan 7311-PH, preamble and Sections 2.01 and 3.02).

philippines-irrigation-canal-easement-re.conditions_add: The loan agreement of 7 August 2009 required the Philippines to implement the project in accordance with the environmental management plans, the land acquisition and resettlement policy framework and the indigenous peoples planning framework, not to amend or waive any provision of them without the Bank's prior approval, and to allocate enough staff and resources to comply (World Bank, Loan Agreement for Loan 7709-PH, Schedule 2, Section I.A.2). Wherever the works would displace people, the agreement required the government to prepare a resettlement action plan under that framework, give it to the Bank for approval, and then implement the approved plan in a manner satisfactory to the Bank (Section I.A.4). The agreement also required the government to maintain an inter-agency steering committee, a project management office and an environmental and watershed management section inside the National Irrigation Administration's central office to monitor safeguards compliance, all with staffing and terms of reference acceptable to the Bank (Section I.A.1).

The same paragraph required that the money be used exclusively for the sub-project it was lent for, and required the fund office to be able to suspend or terminate a local government's right to use the proceeds if it failed to perform its obligations (Schedule 4, paragraph 4(d) and (i)). The additional loan agreement of 12 May 2011 repeated the requirement that the project, including sub-projects, be implemented in accordance with the environmental and social safeguards framework (Loan Agreement for Loan 8035-PH, Schedule 2, Section I.D).

raciborz-polder-nieboczowy-village-remov.conditions_add: The loan agreement of 11 May 2007 required Poland, through the three water management authorities named in it, to carry out the resettlement and rehabilitation plan of August 2005 and the resettlement policy framework "with due diligence and efficiency and at all times provide the funds necessary therefore", to monitor and evaluate that work, and to keep the Bank informed of progress (World Bank, Loan Agreement L7436-PL, Schedule 5, Section B.3). The agreement defined that plan as the measures needed to ensure displaced people were consulted, offered choices among feasible resettlement alternatives, and given prompt and effective compensation at full replacement cost for lost assets. Resettlement costs, including land acquisition and the replacement value of buildings, were an eligible use of the loan proceeds, and the agreement required an independent panel of experts on polder safety, appointed by 31 December 2007 on terms satisfactory to the Bank (Schedule 5, Section B.4).

rwanda-hillside-irrigation-relocation-de.conditions_add: The financing agreement of 8 February 2010 required Rwanda to carry out the project in accordance with the environmental and social management framework, any environmental management plans, the small dam guidelines, any dam safety plans, the resettlement policy framework, any resettlement action plans and the pest management plan, and not to amend, abrogate or waive any of them without the Association's agreement (World Bank, Financing Agreement for Credit 4674-RW, Schedule 2, Section I.D.1). Where those frameworks called for it, the agreement required that a resettlement action plan, environmental management plan or dam safety plan be prepared to the Association's satisfaction and submitted for its review and approval, then adopted and disclosed locally, "prior to implementation" of the sub-project concerned (Section I.D.2). The additional financing agreement of 30 December 2013 repeated these requirements and added a compensation note, defined as listing the land affected, the crops lost, the budget for compensation, a grievance mechanism, the people to be compensated and a certificate of compensation (Financing Agreement for Credit 5360-RW, Schedule 2, Section I.D).

The Bank lent to BOTAS against a guarantee in which the Republic of Turkey "unconditionally guarantees, as primary obligor and not as surety merely" every loan payment (Guarantee Agreement for Loan 8349-TR, Section 2.01).

west-bank-substation-land-taking-eump.conditions_add: The grant agreement of 30 June 2008 required the Palestinian Authority to carry out the project in accordance with the environmental impact assessment, the environmental management plan and the resettlement policy framework, "including the requirement therein to prepare a site-specific Resettlement Action Plan under Part 1 of the Project, in a manner satisfactory to the Administrator, prior to the commencement of works on the respective site" (World Bank, Grant Agreement TF092336, Schedule 2, Section I.E). Part 1 was the substations. The same schedule set financial covenants on the distribution companies: the Jerusalem, Hebron and northern companies had to break even by fiscal year 2009, the southern company by 2010 and the Gaza company by 2011; the Jerusalem company could not borrow unless its forecast internal funds covered at least 1.5 times its debt service and had to keep a self-financing ratio of at least 15 per cent of its average capital spending; and every company's receivables had to fall to three months of average billing by fiscal year 2012. The Bank's completion report records that those financial covenants were eliminated in a restructuring in September 2013.

kasumbalesa-market-traders-moved.conditions_add: The Bank's completion report records one requirement of the original credit agreement for this project: the National Road Fund Agency prepared a plan for its operations after the project "as required under Section 3.3 of the Development Credit Agreement" (World Bank, Implementation Completion and Results Report, 27 April 2015, paragraph 68). The resettlement policy framework for the project was disclosed in October 2003 and the abbreviated resettlement plan for the Kasumbalesa border post in July 2006, both before the only loan agreement the Bank publishes for this project: the additional financing agreement of 12 April 2007, which required that, before civil works involving resettlement or land taking, Zambia "prepare and implement appropriate resettlement plans for compensation, resettlement and rehabilitation of Displaced Persons, in accordance with the Resettlement Policy Framework" (Financing Agreement, Credit 3866-1-ZM, Schedule 4, Section I.B.2).
kasumbalesa-market-traders-moved.ct_note: The credit agreement that paid for the border post works, signed in 2004, is not published. The Bank's document record for the project holds the 2004 appraisal document, the completion report and the 2007 additional financing agreement, but not the original development credit agreement for Credit 3866-ZM, and searches of the Bank's document system by credit number return nothing. What that agreement required is known only from the single section the completion report cites.

kitwe-mufuchani-bridge-relocation.conditions_add: The Bank's completion report says the environmental assessment and resettlement action plans for the Mufuchani bridge "were already reviewed and accepted by the World Bank during RRMP I implementation", that is under the first phase of the road programme, and that 57 houses, two churches and a 1.5 km access road were built in Kitwe for the people moved, with water, sewerage and electricity connections (World Bank, Implementation Completion and Results Report, 26 October 2016, paragraph 36). The first-phase additional financing agreement of 12 April 2007 required that, before any civil works involving resettlement or land taking, Zambia "prepare and implement appropriate resettlement plans for compensation, resettlement and rehabilitation of Displaced Persons, in accordance with the Resettlement Policy Framework"; the resettlement plan for the Mufuchani bridge was disclosed in August 2007 (Financing Agreement, Credit 3866-1-ZM, Schedule 4, Section I.B.2, and the first phase's completion report, Table 4).
kitwe-mufuchani-bridge-relocation.ct_note: The financing agreement for the credit that built the bridge is not published. The Bank's completion report lists the financing agreement of 25 November 2009 for Credit 4654-ZA as a supporting document, but the Bank's record for this project holds 28 documents and no agreement among them, and searches of its document system by credit number and project name return none. The requirement quoted here comes from the first phase's agreement, under which the bridge's resettlement plan was prepared and accepted.
